This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/es/madrid/LEMD.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest forecast consensus from agencies including the UK Met Office and BBC Weather points to a daytime high in Madrid near 33–34°C on August 15, aligning with the market’s tight leading probabilities. This reflects typical late-summer conditions driven by subtropical high pressure, modest southerly flow, and limited cloud cover that allows strong daytime heating without extreme advection of hotter air masses. Small differences between 33°C and 34°C hinge on factors such as exact timing of any scattered showers, local urban heat island effects, and model variations in boundary-layer mixing. With resolution less than 24 hours away, traders are weighting ensemble outputs showing minimal spread around these values rather than outliers near 35°C or below 32°C.

A slightly stronger northerly component or extra sunshine could add 1–2 °C, favoring the upper end of the distribution, while increased cloud cover or a more pronounced sea breeze would cap the reading closer to 17–18 °C.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: The closely matched market odds favoring 31°C (37.5%) or 32°C (36%) reflect persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) conditions over Metro Manila, which are forecast to deliver cloudy skies, scattered rains, and thunderstorms on August 15. These reduce surface solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling amid high humidity typical of the season, limiting peak temperatures near long-term August averages of 31°C. PAGASA guidance shows daily highs in the 30–33°C range without extreme heat buildup, while the absence of clear skies or subsidence prevents stronger warming. Traders weigh model consensus on rainfall timing against any last-minute forecast shifts from official monitoring.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from meteorological models indicate São Paulo’s August 15 maximum will likely reach 24–25 °C under partly cloudy skies and light southeasterly flow typical of winter. Subtle differences among ensemble runs—particularly the timing of any weak frontal boundary and the strength of daytime insolation—create the narrow spread between these two outcomes, which together hold over 56 % of market-implied probability. Official agencies such as INMET and international guidance show low precipitation risk and modest urban heat-island amplification, keeping higher values (26 °C+) at just 23.5 %. Traders appear to weigh the latest model consensus against historical August variability of roughly ±2 °C around the 23–25 °C climatological range, leaving the exact peak sensitive to final observational adjustments before market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus between 26°C and 27°C for Mexico City’s August 15 high stems primarily from ensemble forecasts showing a peak slightly above the long-term August average of 24°C, driven by El Niño-enhanced warmth across central Mexico while typical rainy-season convection caps extremes. Afternoon cloud build-up and scattered showers—common in the monsoon-influenced pattern—introduce key uncertainty, as earlier or heavier precipitation would suppress temperatures toward 25°C or below, whereas delayed or lighter activity could allow brief clearing and push readings to 27–28°C. Mexico City’s high elevation and urban heat island further modulate daily maxima, with model spreads reflecting sensitivity to wind patterns and boundary-layer moisture.
